packet.headline_seed: Meta removes controversial AI feature on Instagram after backlash
packet.description_seed: Meta told Dylan Byers, of Puck News, that it had nixed the feature after backlash from its user base.

what: Meta removes controversial AI feature on Instagram after backlash

clean_source_blocks.text: Meta has axed a controversial feature that allowed users to modify photos from public Instagram accounts using AI. The feature, which was rolled out earlier this week along with a batch of other AI tools, “missed the mark” and is no longer available, according to the company. Earlier this week, Meta announced Muse Image, a new AI image generator built by its dedicated AI unit known as Meta Superintelligence Labs. Meta promoted one feature that allowed individuals to generate images by @-mentioning public Instagram accounts that they wanted to reference. The feature, which wasn’t designed to alert a user if their photos were used in this way, prompted immediate backlash. ---

Meta AI joined the image generation space this week. However, it did so with a controversial default setting that users found upsetting. Meta’s tool allowed anyone to use public Instagram posts as a starting point for creating AI-generated images. Instagram users needed to proactively turn off permission to avoid having their content easily tagged and used for AI image generation. Meta has removed the feature altogether based on user feedback. Dylan Byers at Puck shared a statement from Meta on the decision to pull the feature. Statement from Meta:Earlier this week, we announced that one way for people to generate images in Meta AI is by @-mentioning public Instagram accounts that they want to reference. Our intent was to provide a useful creative tool and to give people control over whether their… ---

According to Meta's policy, anyone with a public Instagram account may see their content used in AI-generated creations without being notified. Users can disable the feature through their privacy settings, but it is enabled by default; adults with public accounts are automatically opted in. The company claims that users can control whether others can produce AI content from their Instagram posts, but critics say that requiring users to opt out rather than asking for explicit consent presents serious privacy concerns. Aside from the controversial Instagram feature, Muse Image provides several AI-powered products, including: Meta also revealed that Muse Video, an AI video-generation model built on the same technology, is now under development. According to Meta, Muse Image incorporates an invisible Content Seal watermark that can identify AI-generated photographs even after they've been cropped, scaled, or screenshotted.

The feature, announced on Tuesday, received significant backlash. The feature, announced on Tuesday, received significant backlash. Following significant backlash, Meta is turning off the feature it announced this week that let users generate AI images based on content from public Instagram accounts just by tagging them. The feature, as originally set up, meant that content from any public Instagram account could be used in AI creations without the account owner’s permission.

original_article.research:
[Lähde: TechCrunch]
Meta has axed a controversial feature that allowed users to modify photos from public Instagram accounts using AI. The feature, which was rolled out earlier this week along with a batch of other AI tools, “missed the mark” and is no longer available, according to the company.

Earlier this week, Meta announced Muse Image, a new AI image generator built by its dedicated AI unit known as Meta Superintelligence Labs. Meta promoted one feature that allowed individuals to generate images by @-mentioning public Instagram accounts that they wanted to reference. The feature, which wasn’t designed to alert a user if their photos were used in this way, prompted immediate backlash.

---

[Lähde: The Verge]
The feature, announced on Tuesday, received significant backlash.

The feature, announced on Tuesday, received significant backlash.

Following significant backlash, Meta is turning off the feature it announced this week that let users generate AI images based on content from public Instagram accounts just by tagging them. The feature, as originally set up, meant that content from any public Instagram account could be used in AI creations without the account owner’s permission.

“Earlier this week, we announced that one way for people to generate images in Meta AI is by @-mentioning public Instagram accounts that they want to reference,” Meta says in an update to a blog post about its new Muse Image AI model. “Our intent was to provide a useful creative tool and to give people control over whether their public content could be referenced in this way. We’ve heard the feedback that this feature missed the mark, so it’s no longer available.”

Meta did let you opt out by digging through settings before turning off the feature entirely, but the feature still drew major criticism.

“Not only does this obviously erode our rights to our own likeness… but it is an obvious tool for #sextortion and other scammers!” Haley McNamara, executive director and chief strategy officer of the National Center on Sexual Exploitation, said earlier on Friday. “Pursuing high-risk design & then putting the onus on individuals to jump through hoops to opt out is unacceptable.”

The Screen Actors Guild recommended that its members opt out of the feature and spelled out instructions on how to do so.

Meta announced on Friday it would be discontinuing an AI tool that let users generate images using public Instagram accounts. This comes just days after the feature's initial rollout, amid mounting criticism.

The company's intention was to offer a creative tool while giving people control over their public content being referenced. However, feedback indicated that the feature did not meet user expectations.

Reacting to the widespread concerns, Meta confirmed the removal of the AI feature, emphasizing its commitment to user feedback and satisfaction.

Meta's recently launched AI image generator, Muse Image, has received widespread criticism after users realized it allows them to create AI images using photos from other users' public Instagram accounts. The internet is fuming with many raising concerns about privacy. A user commented:

Meta Superintelligence Labs launched the feature on July 8, and it is now available through the Meta AI app, Instagram Stories in the United States, and WhatsApp in select countries. While Meta promotes Muse Image as its most advanced image-generation model yet, its ability to recreate other people's public Instagram posts has created an online privacy debate.

To use the feature, one has to simply tag a public Instagram account and type a prompt into the Meta AI app. The AI will then create new images based on the individual's posted photos.

According to Meta's policy, anyone with a public Instagram account may see their content used in AI-generated creations without being notified. Users can disable the feature through their privacy settings, but it is enabled by default; adults with public accounts are automatically opted in.

The company claims that users can control whether others can produce AI content from their Instagram posts, but critics say that requiring users to opt out rather than asking for explicit consent presents serious privacy concerns.

payload.title: Meta poisti kohua herättäneen tekoälyominaisuuden Instagramista
payload.summary: Meta on poistanut ominaisuuden, jolla julkisten Instagram-tilien sisältöä voitiin käyttää tekoälykuvien pohjana pelkän käyttäjätilin mainitsemisen avulla. Yhtiö reagoi käyttäjien arvosteluun pian toiminnon julkaisun jälkeen.
payload.content:
Meta on poistanut tällä viikolla esittelemänsä tekoälyominaisuuden, jonka avulla julkisten Instagram-tilien kuvia voitiin käyttää uusien tekoälykuvien pohjana. Yhtiö teki päätöksen käyttäjiltä saamansa kielteisen palautteen jälkeen ja myönsi ominaisuuden toteutuksen epäonnistuneen tavoitteessaan.

Julkisen Instagram-tilin mainitseminen riitti

Toiminto julkaistiin tiistaina osana Muse Image -kuvageneraattoriin liittyviä tekoälytyökaluja. Muse Imagen on kehittänyt Metan tekoäly-yksikkö Meta Superintelligence Labs. Käyttäjä pystyi pyytämään Meta AI:ta tuottamaan kuvan mainitsemalla @-merkinnällä julkisen Instagram-tilin, jonka julkaisuja haluttiin käyttää uuden kuvan viitteenä.

Alkuperäinen toteutus koski automaattisesti aikuisia käyttäjiä, joilla oli julkinen Instagram-tili. Jos käyttäjä ei halunnut muiden hyödyntävän julkaisujaan tekoälykuvien tekemisessä, hänen piti poistaa lupa itse Instagramin yksityisyysasetuksista. Tilin omistajalle ei myöskään ollut suunniteltu ilmoitusta siitä, että hänen kuviaan oli käytetty tällä tavalla.

Oletusvalinta synnytti yksityisyyshuolia

Käyttäjien ja kriitikoiden arvostelu kohdistui erityisesti siihen, että julkisten tilien sisältö oli käytettävissä ilman tilinomistajan etukäteen antamaa nimenomaista suostumusta. Heidän mukaansa Metan olisi pitänyt pyytää käyttäjiltä lupa ennen julkaisujen hyödyntämistä sen sijaan, että käytön estäminen jäi käyttäjän omalle vastuulle.

Meta kertoi tarkoittaneensa toiminnon hyödylliseksi luovaksi työkaluksi ja halunneensa antaa ihmisille mahdollisuuden hallita sitä, saavatko muut tuottaa tekoälysisältöä heidän Instagram-julkaisuistaan. Yhtiö päätyi kuitenkin käyttäjäpalautteen perusteella poistamaan ominaisuuden kokonaan. Meta kuvaili toteutuksen menneen harhaan tavoitteestaan, eikä toiminto ole enää saatavilla.

Muse-teknologian kehittäminen jatkuu

Kohua herättäneen toiminnon poistaminen ei tarkoita koko Muse Image -kuvageneraattorin vetämistä pois. Metan mukaan generaattorin kuviin sisältyy näkymätön Content Seal -vesileima, jonka avulla tekoälyllä tuotettuja kuvia voidaan tunnistaa myös sen jälkeen, kun niitä on rajattu, niiden kokoa on muutettu tai niistä on otettu kuvakaappaus.

Meta kehittää lisäksi samaan teknologiaan perustuvaa Muse Video -mallia tekoälyvideoiden tuottamiseen. Lähdeaineistossa ei kerrota, aikooko yhtiö palauttaa julkisten Instagram-tilien sisältöä hyödyntäneen toiminnon myöhemmin muutetussa muodossa. Toistaiseksi Metan ilmoittama seuraus käyttäjien vastareaktiosta on ominaisuuden poistaminen, ei pelkästään sen oletusasetusten muuttaminen.
summary_bullets: Poistettu ominaisuus käytti julkisten Instagram-tilien sisältöä tekoälykuvien viitteenä.
Aikuisten julkiset tilit kuuluivat toimintoon oletusarvoisesti, ja käyttö piti estää yksityisyysasetuksista.
Meta poisti toiminnon käyttäjäpalautteen jälkeen mutta jatkaa muiden Muse-työkalujen kehittämistä.
payload.journalist_note: Keskeinen tapahtumakulku on yhdenmukainen neljässä lähdeaineiston osassa. Metan myöhemmistä suunnitelmista poistetun ominaisuuden suhteen ei ole vahvistettua tietoa.

Meta has axed a controversial feature that allowed users to modify photos from public Instagram accounts using AI. The feature, which was rolled out earlier this week along with a batch of other AI tools, “missed the mark” and is no longer available, according to the company. Earlier this week, Meta announced Muse Image, a new AI image generator built by its dedicated AI unit known as Meta Superintelligence Labs. Meta promoted one feature that allowed individuals to generate images by @-mentioning public Instagram accounts that they wanted to reference. The feature, which wasn’t designed to alert a user if their photos were used in this way, prompted immediate backlash. ---

Meta AI joined the image generation space this week. However, it did so with a controversial default setting that users found upsetting. Meta’s tool allowed anyone to use public Instagram posts as a starting point for creating AI-generated images. Instagram users needed to proactively turn off permission to avoid having their content easily tagged and used for AI image generation. Meta has removed the feature altogether based on user feedback. Dylan Byers at Puck shared a statement from Meta on the decision to pull the feature. Statement from Meta:Earlier this week, we announced that one way for people to generate images in Meta AI is by @-mentioning public Instagram accounts that they want to reference. Our intent was to provide a useful creative tool and to give people control over whether their… ---

According to Meta's policy, anyone with a public Instagram account may see their content used in AI-generated creations without being notified. Users can disable the feature through their privacy settings, but it is enabled by default; adults with public accounts are automatically opted in. The company claims that users can control whether others can produce AI content from their Instagram posts, but critics say that requiring users to opt out rather than asking for explicit consent presents serious privacy concerns. Aside from the controversial Instagram feature, Muse Image provides several AI-powered products, including: Meta also revealed that Muse Video, an AI video-generation model built on the same technology, is now under development. According to Meta, Muse Image incorporates an invisible Content Seal watermark that can identify AI-generated photographs even after they've been cropped, scaled, or screenshotted.
